geographic_entities.name: Bahamas
geographic_entities.description: The Bahama Islands extend from the coast of Florida on the north-west to the vicinity of Hayti on the south-east, a distance of 630 miles, and from 22° to 27° 30' N. lat., and from 68° 40' to 79° 30' W. long.

geographic_entities.name: New Providence
geographic_entities.description: The island on which Nassau, the capital, is situated

geographic_entities.name: Nassau
geographic_entities.description: Capital and principal port of the Bahamas, situated on the island of New Providence

geographic_entities.name: Bermudas
geographic_entities.description: Consists of a cluster of small islands surrounded by dangerous reefs
geographic_entities.discovery_details: Discovered by Juan Bermudez, a Spaniard, in 1522

geographic_entities.name: Gibraltar
geographic_entities.description: Fortress and seaport town at the southern extremity of Spain, commanding the entrance to the Mediterranean
geographic_entities.cession_details: Taken by Sir George Rooke, August 4th, 1704; ceded to Great Britain by Treaty of Utrecht, 1713

geographic_entities.name: Heligoland
geographic_entities.description: Small island in the North Sea, 28 miles from the mouth of the Elbe and 36 miles from the nearest point of the mainland of Sleswick
geographic_entities.cession_details: Ceded to Great Britain by Denmark in 1814

geographic_entities.name: British Guiana
geographic_entities.description: Situated on the north-east coast of South America, bounded on the north by the Atlantic Ocean, on the east by Dutch Guiana, on the south and south-west by Brazil, and on the west and north-west by Venezuela

geographic_entities.name: Georgetown
geographic_entities.description: Capital of British Guiana, situated on the right bank of the Demerara River

geographic_entities.name: Cape of Good Hope
geographic_entities.description: British Colony at the southern extremity of Africa
geographic_entities.cession_details: Ceded to Great Britain by the Netherlands in 1814

geographic_entities.name: Cape Town
geographic_entities.description: Capital of the Cape of Good Hope Colony

geographic_entities.name: Ceylon
geographic_entities.description: Large island in the Indian Ocean, separated from India by Palk's Strait
geographic_entities.cession_details: Coastal provinces ceded by Dutch in 1796, Kandyan provinces conquered 1815

geographic_entities.name: Falkland Islands
geographic_entities.description: Group of islands in the South Atlantic, about 300 miles east of the Straits of Magellan

geographic_entities.name: Fiji
geographic_entities.description: Group of islands in the South Pacific Ocean
geographic_entities.annexation_details: Ceded to Great Britain by the native chiefs, October 10, 1874

geographic_entities.name: Griqualand West

geographic_entities.name: British Honduras
geographic_entities.description: British settlement on the east coast of Central America

geographic_entities.name: Hong Kong

area.notes: Hong Kong Island; with Kowloon Peninsula additional

geographic_entities.description: Island and territory on the south coast of China
geographic_entities.cession_details: Island of Hong Kong ceded by Treaty of Nanking, 1842; Kowloon Peninsula ceded 1860

geographic_entities.name: Jamaica
geographic_entities.description: Large island in the Caribbean Sea, south of Cuba
geographic_entities.discovery_details: Discovered by Columbus in his second voyage, May 5, 1494
geographic_entities.conquest_details: Conquered from the Spaniards by Admiral Penn and General Venables, May 10, 1655

geographic_entities.description: Small island off the north-west coast of Borneo
geographic_entities.cession_details: Ceded to Great Britain by the Sultan of Brunei, 1846

geographic_entities.description: Island in the Indian Ocean, about 550 miles east of Madagascar

geographic_entities.name: Freetown
geographic_entities.description: Capital and principal port of Sierra Leone

geographic_entities.name: Gold Coast Colony
geographic_entities.description: British settlements on the Gold Coast of West Africa

geographic_entities.name: St. Vincent

geographic_entities.description: Most southerly of the Windward group, about 20 miles N.E. of Trinidad

geographic_entities.name: St. Lucia

historical_events.description: Discovery of the Bahamas by Christopher Columbus on October 12, 1492
Discovery of Bermuda by Juan Bermudez, a Spaniard
Gibraltar taken by Sir George Rooke on August 4th, 1704
Gibraltar ceded to Great Britain by Treaty of Utrecht
Heligoland ceded to Great Britain by Denmark
Discovery of Natal by Vasco de Gama on Christmas Day, 1497
historical_events.note: Named Natal because discovered on Christmas Day

historical_events.description: District of Natal proclaimed a British Colony by the Governor of the Cape
Natal erected into a distinct and separate Colony, no longer under control of the Governor of the Cape

Langalibalele, chief of the Amalubi Tribe, entered on a contumacious course of conduct ending in attempt to escape with his people and cattle. Colonial force dispatched, tribe subdued, chief transported to Robben Island
First sod turned by the Lieutenant-Governor for railway from Pietermaritzburg to Durban
Fiji ceded to Great Britain by the native chiefs
First settlement of Barbados by Sir William Courteen under protection of Earl of Marlborough, party of 30 persons landed and formed James' (or Hole) Town
4½ per cent duty on all exports abolished by Act of Parliament, four years after abolition of slavery
historical_events.note: This duty had been imposed to satisfy claims of Lord Willoughby and heirs of the two earls

historical_events.description: Discovery of St. Vincent by Columbus on January 22, 1498
5,080 Caribs embarked at Bequia and sailed to Rattan Island in the Bay of Honduras after their surrender
Discovery of Grenada by Columbus, named Ascension
Federation of the Leeward Islands established by Imperial Act 34 & 35 Vict., cap.107
historical_events.note: Revived ancient constitution dating back to William and Mary
